record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Does there exist a real-analytic diffeomorphism of either the annulus T¹ × [-1,1] or the sphere S² that is homotopic to the identity, preserves Lebesgue measure, has only finitely many periodic orbits, and nevertheless has a dense orbit?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a Cω (= R-analytic)-diffeomorphism, homotopic to the identity, Lebesgue measure-preserving, of T1×[-1, 1] or S2, with a finite number of periodic orbits and a dense orbit ?

artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not return evidence of a resolution of this specific question concerning real-analytic, Lebesgue-preserving diffeomorphisms of the annulus or sphere that are homotopic to the identity with finitely many periodic orbits and a dense orbit. Related results (e.g., that any area-preserving annulus homeomorphism with one periodic point has infinitely many) and recent work on mean action of periodic orbits exist but do not directly settle the question, which appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Mean action of periodic orbits of area-preserving annulus diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies action and number of periodic orbits for area-preserving annulus diffeomorphisms; does not resolve the analytic dense-orbit question.
status_evidence.claim: Related modern work on periodic orbits of area-preserving annulus maps does not settle the analytic question.

status_evidence.title: Geodesics on S^2 and periodic points of annulus homeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Classical results show area-preserving annulus homeomorphisms with a periodic point have infinitely many; smooth/analytic case with dense orbit not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Classical constraints do not directly resolve the real-analytic existence question.
